title: Joram’s calf-cult judged less than Baal-statues—because it claimed the true God, wrongly imaged
source_text: XXXII. Ac praeterea idem aperte colligitur, ex iis quae dicuntur de Joram filio Achab, ejusdem libri capite tertio. Sic enim de isto Joram loquitur historicus sacer, Fecit malum coram Domino, sed non sicut pater suus & mater. Abstulit enim statuas Baal quas fecerat pater ejus. Veruntamen in peccatis Jeroboam filii Nabat, qui peccare fecit Israel, adhaesit, nec recessit ab eis. Ubi Spiritus Sancti judicio, quanquam graviter peccaret Rex Joram colens vitulos aureos; peccatum tamen ejus minus grave declaratur, quam peccatum eorum qui statuas Baalis, id est, solis colebant. Unde hoc, nisi quia cultores Baal creaturam simpliciter creatori substituiebant, Solem, scilicet, in suis statuis loco veri Dei colentes; Jeroboam vero & ejus successores, in eo tantum peccabant, quod verum Deum Israel se colere professi, illum colebant in imaginibus, contra voluntatem ejus, ab ipsis excogitatis. Si enim qui colebant vitulos, illos pro diis habebant, aut in iis colebant Apim Aegyptiorum bovem, profecto illorum impietas, hac in parte major adhuc & absurdior erat, quam eorum qui adorabant solem, quo nulla creaturarum visibilium videtur admiratione dignior, & propius Dei imaginem referre.
pass_a_gloss: And besides the same is openly gathered from those things which are said of Joram son of Ahab, in the third chapter of the same book. For thus the sacred historian speaks of that Joram, He did evil before the Lord, but not as his father and mother. For he took away the statues of Baal which his father had made. Nevertheless he cleaved to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, nor did he depart from them. Where by the judgment of the Holy Spirit, although King Joram gravely sinned in cultivating the golden calves; yet his sin is declared less grave than the sin of those who cultivated the statues of Baal, that is, of the sun. Whence this, unless because the cultivators of Baal simply substituted a creature for the creator, cultivating the Sun, namely, in their statues in place of the true God; but Jeroboam and his successors sinned only in this, that having professed to cultivate the true God of Israel, they cultivated him in images, against his will, devised by themselves. For if those who cultivated the calves held them for gods, or in them cultivated Apis the ox of the Egyptians, their impiety in this part would be still greater and more absurd than that of those who adored the sun, than which no visible creature seems more worthy of admiration, and to refer more nearly the image of God.
pass_b_english: Spirit ranks Joram’s calf-sin below Baal-sun worship: calves claimed Jehovah; Baal swapped in a creature.
That ranking collapses if the calves were taken as literal gods or Apis—so relative Jehovah-cult is the better reading, and still condemned.
